entities.summary: Ishāq bin Ali al-Rohawi was a 9th-century author of the first medical ethics book in Arabic medicine. Born in a region that would later become part of the Islamic Golden Age, al-Rohawi's work was instrumental in shaping the medical ethics of the time. His book, which dealt with topics such as patient confidentiality and the treatment of diseases, was widely disseminated throughout the Middle East and North Africa. As a result, al-Rohawi's contributions had a lasting impact on the development of Islamic medical ethics, influencing generations of scholars and physicians. The influence of his work can still be seen in modern medical ethics, where concepts such as informed consent and the duty to protect patients' autonomy originated in part from al-Rohawi's writings. Al-Rohawi's legacy is a testament to the enduring power of Islamic scholarship and its ability to shape the course of human history.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Al-Rohawi's book had a significant impact on the development of medical ethics in the Islamic world, influencing the work of scholars and physicians for centuries to come. Its influence can still be seen in modern medical ethics, where concepts such as informed consent and the duty to protect patients' autonomy originated in part from al-Rohawi's writings.
